einzeiler: Senate candidate Karishma Manzoor on fighting big money and the Democratic establishment
kurzfassung: Dr. Karishma Manzoor discusses her grassroots Senate campaign in New Hampshire and the systemic issues facing American politics. She criticizes both major parties for serving corporate donors rather than working-class citizens. Furthermore, she highlights the challenges of running against heavily funded establishment politicians.
stichpunkte: Karishma Manzoor launched a grassroots Senate campaign in New Hampshire to challenge establishment politicians.
Her platform focuses on Medicare for all, affordable housing, livable wages, and halting foreign weapons transfers.
She criticizes both Democrats and Republicans for taking money from corporate donors and wealthy special interest groups.
Incumbent politicians refused to meet with local peace activists, leading to arrests during peaceful sit-ins.
Private equity firms and wealthy developers are driving a severe housing crisis across the state.
Despite being vastly outspent, her campaign has gained significant traction and shifted the political debate.
She advocates for a lifetime lobbying ban for former members of Congress to curb corruption.

kapitel.titel: Activism and Hitting the Brick Wall
The Housing Crisis and Private Equity

clips.hook: Federal minimum wage stuck for 17 years
clips.text: The federal minimum wage has remained frozen since 2009, and two Democratic senators voted against raising it to fifteen dollars.

clips.hook: New Hampshire faces a massive housing deficit
clips.text: A small state struggles with a deficit of thousands of housing units because developers prioritize luxury mansions over affordable homes.

clips.hook: Elderly citizens and a pregnant official arrested
clips.text: Law enforcement arrested elderly constituents, a church pastor, and a pregnant local official after the congressman refused a meeting.

clips.hook: When party donors wield more power than divine intervention
clips.text: A prominent political figure reversed a firm refusal to drop out of a race shortly after wealthy financial backers threatened to cut off funding.

clips.hook: A massive financial disparity in the Senate race
clips.text: A grassroots challenger operates with a modest budget while facing an opponent backed by millions of dollars.

beschreibung:
The blowback of the failed 2024 Biden-and-then-Harris Democratic presidential campaign, which supported Israel’s genocide in Gaza, continues as another grassroots candidate runs for Congress. Dr. Karishma Manzur, a scientist who is running for senate in the September New Hampshire Democratic Primary against Chris Pappas, joins Chris Hedges in this episode of The Chris Hedges Report to talk about her campaign.

Manzur, who is also an activist for peace and climate justice, has had firsthand experiences with elected officials through her non-profit work, revealing to her the corrosive power of money in politics. She witnessed the ways big donors, such as AIPAC, control the politicians and both political parties, and the corruption and deceit, which she says are most pervasive at the federal level. She finally asked herself, “Why am I being forced to pick the lesser of two evils because the lesser of two evils is still evil. We’re having to choose between bad and really bad.”

Both the Democrats and Republicans engage in anti-democratic practices and demonstrate their allegiance to the wealthy. Manzur criticizes the revolving door between Congressmembers and corporations: “The money in politics is not just bribing our lawmakers and bribing our candidates, these lawmakers themselves are part of the big money.” A major focus for Manzur is what it means to be a public servant. She loathes the culture of treating politicians as celebrities rather than people who work for the public.

Manzur’s campaign rejects corporate donations and is running on a popular program of Medicare for All, affordable housing, living wages and stopping wars, all of which are gaining traction with voters. Despite the Democrat’s efforts to marginalize Manzur and the wide disparity in fundraising between her and her opponent, Manzur is optimistic that she can win.
